title: Client service agreement (editable template)
audience: Owners and office staff who write a written service agreement for recurring or one-off cleaning work, and who need terms that suit Australian practice in their own state or territory
learningOutcomes: Complete each clause so that the client, the business and the team can each state what happens without guessing
Convert any fixed-hours, cancellation or payment term into an Australian term with a workable notice period, and check any term whose legal effect is uncertain before use.
Link each operational term (access, quality, damage, exclusions) to the lesson or schedule that holds its detail

instruction.heading: What an agreement is for
instruction.body: A service agreement records what the business will do, when it will do it, for how long, for what fee, and what happens when something goes wrong. Both parties come back to it when a dispute starts, so each term has to be precise enough to act on. This template is built around a fixed-hours model: the client pays for a reserved block of team hours, not for a promised result. That model can work, but it has to be explained plainly. A client who expects a finished result and receives a time block will feel misled, however accurate the contract is. The scope clause in this template states the difference. The fill-in proposal is “Cleaning proposal for a new client”, the quote terms are in “Quote and proposal”, the access detail is in “Site brief and access sheet for each client”, and the payment detail is in “Payment and overdue account schedule”.

instruction.heading: Converting terms for an Australian business
instruction.body: Several terms in the source model come from a different legal system and must not be carried over. The source sets payment, late-fee, interest, lien, judgment and collection-cost terms that depend on another country's state law, along with a dishonoured-cheque fee and a recovery of legal and collection costs. None of these appear in this agreement. Payment detail sits in “Payment and overdue account schedule”, where each term is checked against the rules in the business's own state or territory before use. Sales tax language is replaced by GST-inclusive pricing. The source presents the business as holding a licence, insurance and a bond, all three. In Australia the business states the insurance it holds and the licences or registrations that apply, with the state or territory where each applies. This template does not confirm that any licence, bond or insurance is required. Clauses that stop a client from hiring the business's own staff can raise competition-law questions, so this template leaves them out. If the business wants one, it takes advice first, and the status of such a clause has not yet been confirmed, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.

instruction.heading: Fixed hours and what the client is paying for
instruction.body: A fixed-hours clause says the client pays for a reserved number of team hours for each visit. Write three things: the reserved hours, the team size, and the rule for finishing early or running over. A team of two working for two hours is not the same as one person working for four hours, and the agreement should say which unit is used. The scope is an activity list that the client can check, and the clause states that the reserved block is the basis of the fee and does not guarantee a result. If the team cannot finish in the reserved time, the clause says what the client is told, how any extra time is approved and how it is charged. Extra time and extra work are agreed in writing before they begin.

instruction.heading: Notice, cancellation and rescheduling
instruction.body: The source sets its own notice periods for cancellation by either party and for schedule details. Those choices belong to one business and are not a standard. Set the notice periods your business can meet from its own roster, and write them as whole numbers of days. Test each one with a single question: could the roster absorb a change at this notice? A period the business cannot meet will not protect it when a job is lost. Where a client's notice is short and the business cannot refill the visit, the clause states the fee and the situation exactly, so that the client knows what applies.

instruction.heading: Access, exclusions, quality and damage
instruction.body: Operational clauses carry the most risk when they are vague. Access details such as keys, lock boxes, alarms and pets belong in the site brief (“Site brief and access sheet for each client”). The agreement refers to that brief and does not hold the detail. Quality is a complaint route with a response time, not a promise that no fault will occur. Damage is handled as a notice, an inspection and a remedy, with the remedy stated as repair, replacement, or a value agreed in writing. The exclusions list states what the business will not do, such as work above a set height, moving heavy items, or handling items the business has not agreed to handle. Each limit is set from the business's own risk assessment. The height and weight figures in the source are not carried over. Check every liability cap or exclusion of responsibility before use, because consumer guarantees may apply.

instruction.heading: Team, insurance, licences and governing law
instruction.body: State who the team are, whether they are employees or subcontractors, and how new team members are trained and supervised. Write the position for this business, and leave it blank until checked. The insurance field lists each policy held, the type of cover, the insurer, the policy number and the expiry date. The licence field lists each licence or registration held that applies to the work, and the state or territory where it applies. Do not list a licence the business does not hold. The governing-law field names the state or territory whose law applies, which is the one where the business operates.

instruction.heading: Keeping the agreement current
instruction.body: Both parties accept the agreement in a way that can be recorded. Record the date, the version number and the name of the person who accepted. An agreement that changes must be reissued with a new version number. The client is told what changed and the date it takes effect, and the business keeps the earlier version on file. A change made verbally is not a change until it is written down and sent.

procedure: Enter the legal and trading names, the ABN, and the client's name, contact details and service address.
State whether the agreement is ongoing or fixed-term, and the start date.
Enter the client's notice period and the business's notice period as whole numbers of days, each checked against the roster.
Describe the service type and list the scope in rows, with the exclusions for each area.
State the reserved team hours, the team size, the schedule and the confirmation method.
Enter the fee with its GST statement, the extra-work approval method, and the reference to the payment schedule.
Describe how price changes are notified, and state that a changed price needs written notice.
Refer to the site brief for access and site rules, and list the exclusions the business applies.
Describe the complaint route, the response time, the damage process and the remedy.
Record the team arrangements, insurance held, licences held, the governing jurisdiction and any referral or feedback terms.
Resolve every open check, or remove the term, then record the version, date and acceptance details.

workedExamples.situation: A client rents out a unit through a booking platform and wants a fortnightly clean booked from the platform's calendar. The platform sometimes changes check-out times at short notice.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which clause decides when the schedule is confirmed, and what should the agreement say when the platform changes a booked time?
workedExamples.reasoning: The schedule clause should say who supplies the schedule, in what form, and how many days before each visit it is needed. A booking platform's calendar is not the client's written instruction, so the agreement should require written confirmation from the client, not a screenshot alone. The clause should then say what happens when the source of the schedule changes: the client sends the new time as a written message, and the business confirms whether it can meet the new time within its notice period. The notice period is set from the business's own roster.

workedExamples.situation: A team member breaks a light fitting while moving a chair to reach a high shelf. The client asks the business to pay for a new fitting and for a replacement chair.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which clauses apply, and what does the agreement say about the notice, the inspection and the remedy?
workedExamples.reasoning: The damage clause applies first: the team member phones the office straight away and leaves a note, and the office follows up in writing to agree the remedy. Moving a chair to reach a shelf may be outside the exclusions for work above a set height, which means the exclusion clause and the business's own risk assessment should be checked. The remedy is repair or replacement, or a value agreed in writing.

equipmentAndPpe: Completed proposal or scope of works (“Cleaning proposal for a new client”, “Scope of works for a commercial cleaning site”)
Site brief for the property (“Site brief and access sheet for each client”)
Payment schedule (“Payment and overdue account schedule”)
Certificate of currency for each insurance policy listed
Licence or registration record for each licence listed
PPE: not applicable to this lesson; the agreement is a document

commonErrors.error: Carrying over a lien, judgment, collection-cost or annual interest term from a non-Australian form.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave these out. Set any payment or debt term in “Payment and overdue account schedule” for the business's own state or territory, and leave it blank until checked.

commonErrors.error: Promising a result in a fixed-hours agreement.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the reserved hours, the team size and the scope, and state that the block of time is the basis of the fee.

commonErrors.error: Stating a licence, bond or insurance cover that the business does not hold.
commonErrors.prevention: Check each entry against the policy or licence document before the agreement is accepted.

commonErrors.error: Setting a notice period the roster cannot meet.
commonErrors.prevention: Test each notice period against the roster and write it as a number the business can keep.

commonErrors.error: Changing a term by phone or in person.
commonErrors.prevention: Put every change in writing, reissue the agreement with a new version number, and record the date the change takes effect.

commonErrors.error: Including a clause that stops the client hiring the team, with a fee attached.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave the clause out unless advice has been taken on its status. Record that advice as pending until it is confirmed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Australian Consumer Law and state or territory fair trading rules: consumer guarantees cannot be excluded for consumers, and unfair contract term rules may apply to standard-form agreements. Check the effect of these rules on each clause against a current source, and record the date.
Payment, late-fee, interest, debt-recovery and lien terms vary by state and territory and are not set in this template.
Check the payroll obligations, workers' compensation and whether team members are employees or subcontractors against the national and state or territory position, and record the date.
Check the types of insurance cover, and whether a client or a state or territory requires a particular cover, against a current source, and record the date.
Height and manual handling limits must come from the business's risk assessment and the work health and safety requirements that apply in the state or territory.

Some cleaning-related work, such as work at height or certain regulated chemicals, may need a licence or authorisation. This lesson covers how to record licences the business holds in an agreement. It does not grant or confirm any licence, and completing it does not authorise any regulated work.

qualityStandard: Every field is completed, or marked not applicable with a reason in the field
Fixed-hours terms state the reserved hours, the team size, the extra-time rule, and that the block of time is not a promise of a result
Each notice period is a whole number of days that the business's roster can meet
Every payment, debt, liability and insurance statement has a recorded check, or has been removed
Each insurance policy and licence listed has a document the business holds
No open check flag remains in the version issued to a client
documentationEvidence: Completed agreement saved with its version number and date
Certificate of currency for each insurance policy listed
Licence or registration record for each licence listed
Record of any change to a term, with the date it takes effect and the version it created
summary: A fixed-hours agreement sells reserved time, not a finished result, and it must say so.
Notice periods are numbers the roster can meet.
Payment and debt detail sits in “Payment and overdue account schedule”, and every unchecked term is flagged.
Insurance and licences are listed only where the business holds a document for them.

editableTemplates.title: Client service agreement
editableTemplates.purpose: A written agreement that sets out the parties, the term, the scope and reserved hours, the fee with its GST position, the notice periods, access and exclusions, quality and damage handling, the team, the insurance and licences held, and the governing jurisdiction. Payment detail is held in the separate schedule “Payment and overdue account schedule”.

fields.label: Business legal and trading name
fields.prompt: Write the legal name of the business, and the trading name if it is different.
fields.guidance: Both names match the registration records the business holds. Where a record cannot be checked, leave the field blank.

fields.label: Business ABN
fields.prompt: Enter the Australian Business Number the business holds.
fields.guidance: Matches the ABN on the registration record. Do not enter a number that has not been checked.

fields.label: Client name and contact details
fields.prompt: Write the client's full name, the contact details for notices, and the name of any other person who may give instructions.
fields.guidance: Notices go to the contact named here. Only people named here may give instructions for the service.

fields.label: Service address
fields.prompt: Write the address where the service is delivered.
fields.guidance: Matches the address on the site brief (“Site brief and access sheet for each client”) for the same property.

fields.label: Term and start date
fields.prompt: State whether the agreement is ongoing or for a fixed period, and the date the first service starts.
fields.guidance: An ongoing agreement says it continues until either party gives notice under the cancellation clause.

fields.label: Client notice to cancel or change
fields.prompt: Enter the number of days' notice the client gives to cancel or change a booked visit.
fields.guidance: A number the business's roster can meet. Any fee for shorter notice is stated with its amount and situation.

fields.label: Business notice to cancel or change
fields.prompt: Enter the number of days' notice the business gives to cancel or change a visit.
fields.guidance: Matches the business's own roster and the commitment it makes to the client.

fields.label: Service type
fields.prompt: Name the service type, for example standard, deep, end of lease, or a custom scope.
fields.guidance: Each type has a scope list in f9. A type with no scope list is not offered.

fields.label: Scope of service
fields.prompt: One row per area. Columns: area, tasks, frequency, exclusions for that area.
fields.guidance: Tasks are actions the client could check. Exclusions in each row match the exclusions field in f15.

fields.label: Reserved hours and team size
fields.prompt: State the reserved team hours for each visit, the headcount on the team, and the rule for finishing early or running over.
fields.guidance: Hours are stated as team hours or person hours, with the team size. The reserved block is the basis of the fee and does not guarantee a result.

fields.label: Schedule and time window
fields.prompt: State the days and the time window, and how the schedule is confirmed in writing before each visit. Check the jurisdiction on record for the business: {{business:compliance.jurisdiction}}.
fields.guidance: The confirmation method and its deadline are stated in days. A change request is made in writing.

fields.label: Fees, GST and extra work
fields.prompt: Enter the fee for each visit, state that it includes GST, and say how extra time or extra work is approved before it starts.
fields.guidance: The fee matches the pricing worksheet (“Pricing and margin worksheet”). Extra fees are approved in writing before work begins.

fields.label: Payment terms reference
fields.prompt: State the payment schedule reference (“Payment and overdue account schedule”) and the invoice method.
fields.guidance: Detailed due dates, overdue steps and charges live in “Payment and overdue account schedule”.

fields.label: Price change notice
fields.prompt: State how the business gives notice of a change to the fee, the notice period in days, and how the client accepts the change or ends the agreement.
fields.guidance: Notice is given in writing before the change takes effect. The notice period is a number.

fields.label: Exclusions and what the business will not do
fields.prompt: List each item, task or type of work the business will not do, with the reason in one line.
fields.guidance: Height and weight limits come from the business risk assessment. Pet care, childcare, and moving appliances or heavy items are listed if they apply.

fields.label: Access, keys and site rules
fields.prompt: Refer to the site brief (“Site brief and access sheet for each client”) and state the key or access method used at the property.
fields.guidance: The key or lock method and the alarm arrangement are recorded in the site brief. Access codes are not written into this agreement.

fields.label: Quality and complaints
fields.prompt: Describe how the client raises a concern, the window they have to raise it, and the response the business gives.
fields.guidance: The complaint window and response time are numbers. The remedy is repair, redo, or another agreed remedy.

fields.label: Damage and incidents
fields.prompt: Describe what the team does if something is damaged, who the client contacts, and how the remedy is agreed.
fields.guidance: Covers the notice, the inspection, the repair or replacement option and how any value is agreed in writing.

fields.label: Team, supervision and conduct
fields.prompt: State who the team are, whether they are employees or subcontractors, how new team members are trained and supervised, and the conduct rules the team follows in the home.
fields.guidance: Employee or subcontractor status is stated. Conduct rules are listed only where the business enforces them.

fields.label: Insurance held
fields.prompt: List each insurance policy the business holds: type of cover, insurer, policy number and expiry date.
fields.guidance: Each policy is backed by a certificate of currency. Do not list cover the business does not hold.

fields.label: Licences and registrations held
fields.prompt: List each licence or registration the business holds that applies to the work, and the state or territory where it applies.
fields.guidance: Each entry is checked against the document. If you are not sure whether a licence applies, leave it blank and check with the relevant authority.

fields.label: Governing law and disputes
fields.prompt: Name the state or territory whose law governs the agreement, and the first step for a dispute.
fields.guidance: The state or territory is the one where the business operates. The dispute steps are stated. The legal wording has not yet been confirmed, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.

fields.label: Changes, feedback and referrals
fields.prompt: State any referral or feedback arrangement the business offers, and how changes to the agreement are recorded.
fields.guidance: Any referral credit states its amount, its condition and when it applies. The feedback route matches f17.

fields.label: Signatures and acceptance
fields.prompt: Record the client's name, the business representative's name, the date of acceptance, and the version number of this agreement.
fields.guidance: Acceptance is by a method the business can keep. The version number changes when any term changes.

levels.meets: Legal and trading names, ABN, client contact, service address, term and start date are all present and checked.
levels.does_not_meet: Any of these is missing, or an ABN or name has not been checked against a record.

levels.meets: Reserved hours, team size, the extra-time rule and the statement that the block is not a promise of a result are all present.
levels.does_not_meet: Hours are given without the team size, the extra-time rule is missing, or the agreement promises a result.

levels.meets: Each notice period is a whole number of days that the roster can meet, and the reason is recorded.
levels.does_not_meet: A notice period is missing, is not a number, or cannot be met from the roster.

levels.meets: No lien, judgment, collection-cost, annual interest, cheque-return fee or non-Australian state law term appears in the agreement.
levels.does_not_meet: Any such term appears in the agreement.

assessmentRubric.criterion: Insurance and licences are backed by records

levels.meets: Each insurance policy and licence listed has a document the business holds, with its number and expiry date.
levels.does_not_meet: A policy or licence is listed with no record, or a licence is listed that the business does not hold.

levels.meets: Each item still to be checked has been checked and resolved, or removed, and the check is recorded before issue.
levels.does_not_meet: No open check flag remains in the version issued to a client.

officialReferences.title: Consumer rights and guarantees
officialReferences.pageDate: no date shown in body text (page metadata: published and modified 28 August 2026)
officialReferences.covers: States that the basic consumer guarantee rights cannot be taken away by anything a business says or does, and that it is against the law for a business to mislead consumers about those rights, for example with a 'no refunds' sign. Does not address unfair contract terms, liability caps, payment terms, governing law, payroll or workers' compensation; states that consumer guarantees do not apply to financial products such as insurance. Publisher: ACCC.
